question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186124473/plots/plot-3881d9f51b525d9e7a66d7f58ac7b1a12701c837349c9ef53e0dbd144c65ba98.png)

On which of the following intervals is the function $f(x)$ (shown above) invertible?

I. $x\in [1,3]$

II. $x\in [0,3]$

III. $x\in (-2,1]$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

- On interval I, $x\in [1,3]$, the function is invertible. Indeed, any horizontal line will intersect the restricted graph at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

- On interval II, $x\in [0,3]$, the function is **not** invertible. Some horizontal lines will intersect the restricted graph more than once.

- On interval III, $x\in (-2,1]$, the function is invertible. Indeed, any horizontal line will intersect the restricted graph at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".
